id.description: Stable internal key. Never displayed; safe to keep when a name is corrected.

name.description: Display name as spelled in the primary text where possible.

alias.description: A second name the Bob actually goes by in the text. Jeremy goes by Morlock; use this rather than renaming the record, so both are searchable.

parent.description: id of the source Bob. Omit entirely for tier C (no lineage on record). For tier P this is an ancestor, not necessarily a direct parent.

src.description: How well we know this Bob's PARENTAGE, and nothing else. t=parent confirmed in the books; a=Taylor's 2017 tree; b=fandom wiki registry; p=an ancestor is known but the generations between are not; c=no ancestor on record; x=the record was deliberately expunged. A tier C Bob can still be richly documented — Herschel states his own generation on the page and has twenty POV chapters; we just don't know who made him. Tier X is narrower and stronger: we know why the data is missing, because somebody removed it on purpose. Reserve it for cases the text actually accounts for; requires a cite and a partialNote.

cite.description: Chapter reference for whatever this record's strongest textual claim is. Required for tier T, where it must support the parent link. Welcome on any tier — a tier C Bob may still have a citable generation, death, or first appearance. Format: 'Bk<n> ch<n> · <POV>, <date>'.

gen.description: Generation as stated in a source. May disagree with drawn tree depth when the parent is unknown; the app shows both.

desig.description: In-universe designation, and the Bob's actual identity — they all wear the same face, so Guppy identifies them by serial number or not at all (Bk3 ch21). Two schemes: 'Bob-<n>' for the early global numbering, abandoned once coordinating numbers between star systems got unwieldy (Bk1 ch28); and 'HIC<catalogue>-<n>' after, where the Hipparcos Catalog number names the system the Bob was built in and <n> is the index within it (Bk1 ch15). The validator checks HIC prefixes against origin.

origin.description: System where this Bob was built.

lostAt.description: Where destroyed or last known, when status is lost.

faction.description: Affiliation, not lineage. The four mutual-interest groups Bill describes as forming once replicative drift made Bobs into 'joiners'. Deliberately separate from the tree because factions cut across branches — Starfleet took joiners from other lines and purged its own genealogy records, so it can never be drawn as a subtree.

conflict.description: Describe the disagreement between sources and which one the tree follows.

partialNote.description: For tier P: exactly what the source does and doesn't say about the gap.

note.description: Prose shown in the detail panel.
